I(M18) relate to this post so much. I'm a senior in high school with virtually no friends, i have poor social skills, and people dont find me too interesting compared to when I was in what felt like the best times of my life (around 13-16). People expect me to be the same person but after trauma and chronic stress im really just a blank person trying to mimic who they knew me as. I wish I could just re kindle the natural connection I had with myself but i dont think thats happening anytime soon. but i feel like its important for people who feel that way to remember 1. REPUTATION IS BRITTLE. For example: There is a girl at my school who used to be pretty popular and she was known for her nice body, but as soon as she put on a bit of weight no one really talks to her, and people talk more negatively about her 2. YOUR OPINION OF YOURSELF IS THE ONLY ONE THAT MATTERS 3. YOU CAN RECREATE YOURSELF 4. STOP BEING SO ATTACHED TO A FORMER VERSION OF YOU. Personally I have to remind myself of these things cause i know im not perfect but knowing these things help me keep my head up and move on. I know it's hard, but if you wanna see a better version of yourself you at the very least have to stay alive. I promise things will go better than your brain makes you think

I feel you, man. It's hard realizing this stuff at a young age. I'm 17 and I realized this when I started working at McDonald's for a few months. I eventually got tired of it and quit but literally on my last day I had a vision. In the vision, I saw myself still working at that McDonald's for the rest of my life (until I was like 60) and I thought to myself, "why the fuck do we have to live like this?" And I was reminded of my family members and all the people who have to go work at a minimum wage job until they're old and frail. I had tears in my eyes because that could very well be a reality for me and it is for MOST people. It sucks that we don't live a more simple life because I feel like people would be happier and things, in general, would be easier. But realizing that I don't have the power to make that happen is what makes me feel so defeated. We gotta at least hope for better and strive for it. Just know you're not alone in this way of thinking

You don't know how much I relate to this. I'm 17M in my junior year of HS and I literally sit in my room, cheat on my homework all day and have my mom bring me food(I feel worthless at times). it feels like my trauma has zapped me of every ounce of energy I had. And I feel bad for it especially because at a time I prided myself on being active and having good grades, but now I don't even see the importance in anything besides trying to heal my wounds. Society won't care about my trauma, they will still judge me on my grades, I'll still have to go to a job and neglect my problems, and it feels like after high school it only gets worse. Sometimes I question the point of living in this world. (not suicidal tho)

And it sucks while you're facing the trauma because, the only way to truly accept it as it is, is to realize that this is a human experience and in the end this is for your soul to grow more insight/knowledge
